X.note: The wall textures and light are strong, but the people look like flat cardboard cutouts or game sprites. They have uniform grey and blue colours and no contact shadows to match the strong sun. Some of the figures hover. The grime on the left wall is overdone and looks like a texture smear. The ship in the distance is a tiny blob.

Y.note: Atmospheric haze, warm backlight and cooler shadows give depth. The walls have cornices, string courses and stone plinths, which look more like real architecture. The crowd is silhouetted and hazed, so it reads as people in light fog and the weak figure modelling is hidden. The figures are still generic, faceless and uniform, with no visible uniform detail. The sunlit cobbles are a bit too orange. The ship is a little clearer.

why: Haze and silhouetted figures hide the weak character models, and the richer building detail and depth make it look closer to a real documentary frame.
top_fix_for_weaker: Replace the flat, evenly lit sprite crowd in X with properly modelled figures. Give them period uniforms (khaki drill, naval whites, civilians in hats). Add contact shadows that match the low sun, vary their height and spacing, and add atmospheric haze toward the harbour. Tone down the grime on the left wall and add cornices and plinths like Y's.
anachronisms_seen: Pale blue box or kiosk at the end of the right-hand street, purpose unclear
Uniform grey and blue figures that don't match 1943 British khaki or whites
Union Jack flag shown at full size with no hint of wartime context
Modern-looking recessed black window frames and dark rectangular openings
